title: A released version can be labelled, and the labels are published; no path moves latest
git-semver reads and writes git-deps.labels.json in a documented, versioned format
body:
Part of epic gsv-3226 (unit 7 of plan git-dev-aef7; design in mangimangi/git-dev .pearls/docs/how-versions-move-design.md, section 'Words and shapes settled on 2026-11-28'). Delivers into plan/git-dev-aef7 on top of v0.1.2. Re-check every code reference before using it.

## Goal
A labels file, git-deps.labels.json at the repository root (whoever keeps the default branch vouches for it; git-deps reads it through git, nothing here calls a platform). This issue adds only the reader/writer, its schema/reference and docs. The subcommands that use it are a separate issue (label/unlabel/labels) that depends on this one.

Settled, do not reopen: the word is 'label' (not mark/advisory/tag; 'tag' means a version tag only); labels are a file, not git tags; a pin is a version and a sha; the format must carry labels this unit does not define (e.g. eol, or a positive one later) and a reader must ignore a label it does not know.

## Format (decided in refinement; record it in README as the contract)
{
  "format": 1,
  "versions": {
    "v0.1.2": [
      {"name": "defect", "reason": "one line", "date": "2026-11-28", "commit": "<40-hex sha the tag pointed at>", "fixed_in": "0.1.3"}
    ],
    "backend/v2.3.0": [ ... ]
  }
}
- 'format' is an integer format version; this unit defines 1. A file with a higher format is refused with a message naming the supported format.
- 'versions' is keyed by the full version tag name exactly as format_tag() in git-semver produces it (vX.Y.Z for the root, <subdir>/vX.Y.Z for a subdirectory component) and must match VERSION_TAG_RE (git-semver, defined just above cmd_released). Decision: keying by tag name covers per-component labels in one flat map, with no second nesting level, and is what a reader already sees in `git tag`.
- Each label: 'name' (string, required), 'commit' (40-hex string, required), 'date' (YYYY-MM-DD UTC, required), 'reason' (one-line string; required by the command for defect, optional when reading), 'fixed_in' (optional X.Y.Z version of the same component).

## Reading: strict about structure, tolerant about content
Add a constant LABELS_FILE = "git-deps.labels.json" and functions in git-semver (e.g. load_labels(path) / dump_labels(data) / save_labels(path, data); place them in a new '# ── Labels ──' section before '# ── Subcommands ──'). A missing file reads as empty ({format: 1, versions: {}}).
Raise SemverError naming what is wrong (and where, e.g. the tag key and label index) for: invalid JSON; top level not an object; 'format' missing, not an int, or greater than 1; 'versions' missing or not an object; a key that is not a version tag; a value that is not a list; a list item not an object; missing/ill-typed name, commit (not 40-hex), date (not YYYY-MM-DD); reason not a string (or containing a newline); fixed_in not an X.Y.Z version (use parse_version).
Kept and ignored: an unknown label name (anything besides 'defect'), unknown fields on a label, unknown top-level keys. All of these are written back unchanged.

## Writing: stable under version control
- json with indent 2, trailing newline, ensure_ascii=False.
- Top-level key order: format, versions, then unknown keys in the order read.
- 'versions' keys sorted by component (root first, then subdir name) then by version precedence (parse_version), not lexically.
- Labels within a version sorted by name; label keys in the fixed order name, reason, date, commit, fixed_in, then unknown fields in the order read.
- Load then save of a file already in canonical form is byte-identical (nothing untouched is reordered).

## Schema/reference
Add templates/labels.schema (JSON Schema, alongside templates/config.schema; follow its style) describing format 1, with additionalProperties allowed so unknown fields remain valid. Decision: add "templates/labels.schema" to "files" in .vendored/configs/git-semver.json (allowed config file), because every other file under templates/ is listed there and a change to the published contract should bump the version.

## Docs
- README.md: new section 'Labels (git-deps.labels.json)' (after the 'git-semver released' section): what a label is, where the file lives, the format with the example above, field table, the strict/tolerant rules, the stability rules, and that 'latest' is computed by a reader (newest version no label rules out), not a tag. State it is the contract a reader such as git-deps relies on and point to templates/labels.schema.
- AGENTS.md Key Files: mention templates/labels.schema / the labels file.

## Version
This epic adds commands, so the pull request into plan/git-dev-aef7 raises the version one minor step (0.1.2 -> 0.2.0) once. Decision: whichever of this epic's issues lands first on the impl branch runs `./git-semver bump minor --no-push` (VERSION still equals origin/main's 0.1.2); later issues add their line to the existing [0.2.0] CHANGELOG.md entry instead of bumping again. This issue's changelog line: 'git-deps.labels.json: a documented, versioned labels file (format 1) git-semver reads and writes'.

## Tests
New tests/test_labels.py following tests/test_commands.py / tests/test_config.py patterns (tmp_repo fixture in tests/conftest.py; no token, no network). Cover: missing file reads empty; round trip of the README example is byte-identical; an unknown label name and an extra label field and an extra top-level key are read without error and written back preserved; each malformed case above raises SemverError with a message naming the problem; higher format refused; sorting (versions by precedence v0.10.0 after v0.9.0, root before subdirs; labels by name; field order). Every new line covered (coverage >= 99% for git-semver and release).

## Acceptance criteria
- load/save functions and LABELS_FILE exist with the behaviour above; templates/labels.schema exists and is listed in files.
- A file with an unknown label name and an extra field is read without error and written back with both preserved; a structurally malformed file is refused with a message.
- README documents the format with an example; CHANGELOG/VERSION per the Version section.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup` passes (coverage >= 99% for both scripts, bats green); `git-semver check-bump --no-fix` passes against origin/main; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` reports nothing (no vendor-protected file added, changed or deleted).

title: git-semver label / unlabel / labels: label a released version, withdraw a label, list labels
body:
Part of epic gsv-3226 (unit 7 of plan git-dev-aef7). Delivers into plan/git-dev-aef7. Depends on gsv-3226.1 (the labels file reader/writer: LABELS_FILE = git-deps.labels.json, load_labels/save_labels, format 1 keyed by full tag name vX.Y.Z or <subdir>/vX.Y.Z, label fields name, reason, date, commit, fixed_in). Re-check every code reference before using it.

## Goal
Three new subcommands in git-semver, defined beside cmd_tag and cmd_released (git-semver ~line 946 and ~1015) and registered in build_parser() and the command dispatch. None of them commits, pushes, tags, reads a config file's 'files', needs a token or the network: they change (or read) git-deps.labels.json in the working tree root (git rev-parse --show-toplevel), and the change reaches the default branch as any other change does.

## git-semver label <version> defect --reason "..." [--fixed-in <version>] [--subdir <name>]
- <version> accepts X.Y.Z or vX.Y.Z; the tag is format_tag(version, subdir).
- Refuses (SemverError, exit 1) a version that has no tag: resolve with `git rev-parse --verify <tag>^{commit}`; records that commit (40-hex) as 'commit'.
- 'defect' requires --reason (non-empty, one line, no newline); missing reason fails.
- Decision: label accepts only the name 'defect' and refuses any other name with a message saying defect is the only label git-semver makes. Reason: the epic scopes labels other than defect out ('Labels other than defect as things git-semver knows how to make' is out of scope); unknown labels in the file are still preserved and can be removed with unlabel.
- --fixed-in must be a tagged version of the same component (format_tag(fixed, subdir) resolves) and strictly higher than the labelled version (parse_version comparison); otherwise fails naming why.
- 'date' is today's UTC date (YYYY-MM-DD).
- Idempotent: labelling a version that already has a label with the same name updates its reason and fixed_in (omitting --fixed-in keeps an existing fixed_in) without duplicating. Decision: the original 'date' and 'commit' are kept on update, because they record when the label was made and what the tag pointed at then. Unknown fields on the existing label are preserved.
- Prints what it did ('Labelled v0.1.2 defect' / 'Updated defect on v0.1.2') and that the file must be committed and reach the default branch through a pull request.

## git-semver unlabel <version> <name> [--subdir <name>]
- Accepts any name (so a label git-semver does not define can be withdrawn too); does not require the tag to exist.
- Removes the label; drops the version key when its list becomes empty. Decision: when the file is left with no versions and no unknown top-level keys, the file is deleted, so label then unlabel restores the working tree exactly whether or not the file existed before.
- When there was no such label it says so ('No defect label on v0.1.2') and exits 0. Decision: exit 0 keeps removal idempotent, matching how cmd_tag treats an existing tag.

## git-semver labels [<version>] [--subdir <name>] [--json]
- Lists labels for all versions, or one version, in a readable form: one line per label, e.g. 'v0.1.2  defect  2026-11-28  <short sha>  fixed in 0.1.3  — <reason>', in the file's canonical order; unknown label names are listed too. Prints nothing (exit 0) when there are none.
- --json prints the (filtered) file content as JSON in the canonical form gsv-3226.1 writes.
- A malformed file is an error with the reader's message.

## Docs
- README.md: a section per command under the commands reference (after 'git-semver released'), with flag tables in the existing style, plus 'Labelling a release' showing the whole path for a repository with a protected default branch: create a branch, run `git-semver label 0.1.2 defect --reason "..." --fixed-in 0.1.3`, commit git-deps.labels.json, open a pull request, merge. Note that git-deps.labels.json is not one of the configured 'files', so labelling does not ask for a version bump (check-bump does not fire).
- AGENTS.md: add label/unlabel/labels to the git-semver row of the Key Files table.
- CHANGELOG.md: line in the [0.2.0] entry ('label, unlabel and labels subcommands record, withdraw and list labels of released versions'). If VERSION still equals origin/main's 0.1.2 when this lands, run `./git-semver bump minor --no-push` first (the epic raises the version one minor step once; see gsv-3226.1).

## Tests
Extend tests/test_labels.py (from gsv-3226.1) with tests that use real local git repositories only (tmp_repo fixture in tests/conftest.py, git init + commits + annotated tags; no token, no network), plus CLI-level tests via build_parser/main as tests/test_commands.py does. Cover:
- labelling a tagged version writes the file with name, reason, date (today UTC) and the tag's commit; v-prefixed and plain versions both work; --subdir writes <subdir>/vX.Y.Z;
- labelling an untagged version fails; defect without reason fails; non-defect name fails;
- --fixed-in that is untagged, equal, or lower fails; a higher tagged one is recorded;
- repeating the label updates reason/fixed_in without duplicating and keeps date/commit;
- unlabel restores the file byte-identically (with a pre-existing file) and deletes it when it was created by label; unlabel of a missing label says so and exits 0; unlabel of an unknown name works;
- labels prints human output and --json; filter by version; nothing for empty;
- no command creates a commit, tag or push (assert git log/tag unchanged).
Coverage >= 99% for git-semver and release.

## Acceptance criteria
- Labelling a tagged version writes the file with the label, reason, date and the tag's commit; labelling an untagged version fails; a defect without a reason fails; a fixing version that is not a higher tagged version fails; repeating a label updates it without duplicating; removing it restores the file — shown by tests using local repositories only.
- labels lists readable output and JSON with --json.
- README and AGENTS.md updated as above.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup` passes (coverage >= 99% for both scripts, bats green); `git-semver check-bump --no-fix` passes against origin/main; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` reports nothing.

title: No git-semver path creates or moves a latest tag or force-pushes tags
body:
Part of epic gsv-3226 (unit 7 of plan git-dev-aef7). Delivers into plan/git-dev-aef7. Independent of gsv-3226.1/.2. Re-check every code reference before using it.

## Problem
git-semver still force-moves a 'latest' git tag on the bump-on-merge path. The planning doc cited git-semver lines 625, 700 and 760 at v0.1.1; at v0.1.2 (current) they are:
- cmd_bump: git-semver:862 `git("tag", "-f", "latest")`, 863 `print(f"Tagged: {tag} + latest")`, 867 `git("push", "--tags", "--force", check=True)`
- cmd_bump_all: git-semver:937 tag -f latest, 938 'Tagged: {tags_str} + latest', 942 push --tags --force
- cmd_tag: git-semver:996-997 '# Always update latest tag' + tag -f latest, 1004 'Created tags: {tags_str} + latest', 1007 push --tags --force (under --push)
A moved tag makes `git fetch --tags` fail in every clone that holds the old one ('would clobber existing tag'). The owner decided to drop it; the pull request mode (release with bump_on pull_request, release:525 `git push origin <tag>`) already does not move it. 'latest' is computed by a reader (newest version no label rules out), not a tag.

## Change
- Remove all three `git("tag", "-f", "latest")` calls and the '+ latest' / 'Always update latest tag' text; messages become 'Tagged: <tags>' / 'Created tags: <tags>'.
- Replace every `git push --tags --force` with pushing only the tags this run created, by name, without force: `git push origin <tag>` per tag (same as release's tag-on-merge path). Decision: push by name rather than plain `git push --tags`, because --tags would also try to push a stale local 'latest' (or any other local tag) and fail on 'would clobber'. cmd_bump/cmd_bump_all still push the commit first with `git push`.
- An existing 'latest' tag in a repository is left alone (never deleted; deleting it is the owner's choice) and ignored wherever tags are read as versions: keep get_latest_tag_version's v[0-9]* pattern, VERSION_TAG_RE in cmd_released, and release:181 create_releases skipping 'latest' (keep that filter, it protects repositories that still hold one).
- release (docstring ~line 28) and any message there that mentions latest: update so no path is described as moving latest.
- install.sh already fetches from the v$VERSION tag (fetch_file default ref) and README line 26 already reads the script from main; verify nothing in install.sh, templates/ (templates/github/workflows/version-bump.yml, templates/AGENTS.md) or docs relies on a 'latest' ref, and that bootstrap instructions name a version or the default branch.

## Docs
- README.md: bump step 7 (line ~117) 'Creates annotated tag ... + updates latest tag' -> no latest; step 8 pushes the commit and the new tag by name; 'git-semver tag' bullet 'Always creates/updates the latest tag' (~144) removed and the --push row '(git push --tags --force)' (~147) becomes 'push each created tag by name, never forced'; 'Two ways to release' table row 'latest tag | created and moved | not created or moved' (~436) becomes not created or moved on either path; the bullet at ~452 generalised. Add a short note: an existing latest tag is left alone and ignored; delete it with `git push origin :refs/tags/latest` and `git tag -d latest` if you want; pin a version or read the default branch instead.
- AGENTS.md line 42 ('does not move the latest tag') stays true; adjust wording if needed so it does not imply other paths move it.
- CHANGELOG.md [0.2.0] entry, Changed: 'latest is no longer created or moved on any path and tags are never force-pushed; a repository or script that fetched from the latest ref names a version tag (vX.Y.Z) or the default branch instead, and an existing latest tag is left in place and ignored'. If VERSION still equals origin/main's 0.1.2 when this lands, first run `./git-semver bump minor --no-push` (the epic raises the version one minor step once; see gsv-3226.1).

## Tests
- Update tests/test_commands.py assertions that expect latest: line ~190 ('Tagged: v1.0.1 + latest'), ~195 and ~546 (`("tag", "-f", "latest") in git_cmds`) now assert it is absent; assert no git call contains '--force' and that tags are pushed as ('push', 'origin', '<tag>'). Keep the tests that a pre-existing latest is ignored (test_commands.py ~739-797; test_bump_and_release.py create_releases cases with 'latest' in stdout).
- Add integration tests with real local repositories and a local bare remote (pattern of tests/test_tag_on_merge.py, which already asserts `g(repo, "tag", "-l", "latest") == ""` at ~116): after a bump-on-merge release (release bump / bump-all + tag --push path, and git-semver bump without --no-push) and after a tag-on-merge release, no 'latest' tag exists in the clone or the remote that git-semver made; a pre-existing 'latest' at an old commit in the remote and clone is unchanged after the release (proves nothing moved it and no force push happened, and the release does not fail on it). No token, no network.
- If install.sh changes, add a bats test in tests/bats/install.bats.
Coverage >= 99% for git-semver and release.

## Acceptance criteria
- grep finds no `tag", "-f"` or `--force` push in git-semver or release; no path creates, moves or pushes latest.
- After a bump-on-merge release and after a tag-on-merge release in a test repository, no latest tag exists that git-semver made, and no push used force.
- README, CHANGELOG (and VERSION at 0.2.0) updated as above; installer and docs do not rely on a latest ref.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup` passes (coverage >= 99% for both scripts, bats green); `git-semver check-bump --no-fix` passes against origin/main; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-aef7` reports nothing; release bump, release publish, the two release modes and check-bump are otherwise unchanged.
